description: AER reported high electricity demand together with bushfire-related network outages in NSW on 4 January; the report does not provide a demand MW value for this event.

event_name: NEM COVID-19 demand change - 1 Apr-17 May 2020
description: COVID-19 restrictions changed electricity use across the NEM from 1 April to 17 May 2020: commercial demand fell while residential demand rose. Across Q2, AEMO estimated a 2.1% NEM operational-demand reduction attributable to COVID-19; reductions were largest in New South Wales and Queensland, while South Australian operational demand increased as cooler-weather residential heating offset commercial reductions.
supporting_source_title: AEMO COVID-19 demand impact in Australia
supporting_source_note: The former NSW and Victoria rows described the same national restriction episode and were consolidated. The 1 April-17 May window follows the exact interval printed under AEMO Figure 4; the report documents NEM-wide and regional demand effects.

event_name: NEM winter minimum demand record - 29 Aug 2020
description: At 13:30 on 29 August, NEM operational demand reached a then-record winter daytime minimum of 15,365 MW. In the same interval and under the same mild, sunny, high-rooftop-PV conditions, South Australia and Victoria also set winter minimum operational-demand records of 585 MW and 3,448 MW.
source_title: AEMO A record breaking winter weekend
supporting_source_note: The separate South Australian row was removed because AEMO reports the NEM and regional records as one simultaneous record-setting event.

description: At 12:30 on 11 October South Australian operational demand fell to 300 MW, 158 MW below the 2019 minimum; total solar generation was equivalent to 100% of underlying demand during the interval.
supporting_source_note: Same 11 October event: AER reports 318 MW daily minimum native demand, while AEMO reports 300 MW operational demand. Values differ because the demand definitions differ.

event_name: NEM December solar and mild-weather demand erosion
description: During December 2020, mild early-summer conditions reduced daytime cooling demand while record distributed-PV growth continued to erode midday NEM operational demand; AEMO reported the largest PV-output increases in New South Wales and Queensland.
supporting_source_note: December is used instead of the full quarter because AEMO singles it out for reduced cooling demand, and AER reports exceptionally mild southern conditions, high rooftop-solar output and record-low prices in the week beginning 6 December.

description: On 14 March South Australian operational demand fell to 347 MW. AEMO issued Market Notice 83319 at 08:17 and a clause 4.8.9 instruction at 14:31; 71 MW of distributed PV was curtailed and demand returned above 400 MW at 14:43.
source_title: AEMO Maintaining operational demand in South Australia on 14 March 2021
supporting_source_title: AEMO Solar PV curtailment initiative by SA Government supports the NEM
supporting_source_note: AEMO media release describing the same 14 March 2021 intervention; the incident report is retained as the primary source because it contains the market-notice number and detailed timeline.

description: AEMO reported that strict NSW COVID-19 restrictions combined with unusually warm August weather reduced average underlying demand by 394 MW compared with August 2020, particularly during the 06:30–08:30 morning peak.
At 12:30 on 19 September NSW operational demand reached 4,872 MW, its lowest level since Q1 2000; distributed PV supplied 2,722 MW, or 36% of underlying demand.
At 14:00 on 26 September South Australian operational demand reached a record minimum of 236 MW; distributed PV supplied 1,131 MW, equivalent to 83% of underlying demand.
supporting_source_note: Same 26 September event: AER reports 265 MW daily minimum native demand, while AEMO reports 236 MW operational demand. AER also attributes the record to warmer spring conditions and record rooftop solar output.

description: At 13:00 on 17 October, NEM operational demand reached a record minimum of 12,936 MW, with distributed PV supplying 40% of NEM underlying demand. New South Wales simultaneously set a regional minimum of 4,425 MW, so the event is recorded once at NEM level.
supporting_source_note: AEMO reports the NEM and New South Wales records at the same 17 October interval; the row is therefore classified as NEM rather than NSW1.

description: South Australian operational demand reached a then-record minimum of 188 MW on 31 October as high rooftop solar output displaced grid-supplied operational demand.
source_title: AEMO Negative electricity demand in South Australia

description: At approximately 13:00 on 21 November South Australian operational demand reached 104 MW; distributed PV supplied approximately 1,220 MW, or 92% of underlying demand.
At 13:00 on 3 April South Australian operational demand reached its Q2 minimum of 346 MW; distributed PV supplied 1,473 MW, equivalent to 77% of underlying demand.
Cold conditions increased electricity demand across the NEM between 7 and 12 June; maximum operational demand was more than 1 GW higher on average than during the preceding week.
source_title: AEMO NEM market suspension and operational challenges in June 2022

event_name: NEM spot market suspension begins - 15 Jun 2022
description: AEMO suspended the NEM spot market at 14:00 AEST on 15 June 2022. The suspension was formally lifted at 14:00 AEST on 24 June; that later date is duration context, while the recorded event date is the documented start.
supporting_source_title: AEMO NEM market suspension and operational challenges in June 2022
supporting_source_note: Both official sources identify 15 June 2022 as the start of the suspension. The 24 June lifting date is retained in the description but is not used as the event date.

event_name: NEM winter minimum demand record - 28 Aug 2022
description: On 28 August NEM operational demand reached a new winter minimum of 14,159 MW as increasing rooftop solar output reduced daytime grid demand.
source_title: AEMO New low winter demand records observed while solar generation continues to rise

description: At 13:00 on 16 October South Australian operational demand reached a record minimum of 100 MW, with distributed PV supplying approximately 93% of underlying demand.
At 13:00 on 29 October NSW operational demand reached a record minimum of 4,356 MW; the same minimum was recorded again on 30 October.
supporting_source_note: Same 29 October event: AER reports 4,483 MW daily minimum native demand and a second native-demand low of 4,498 MW on 30 October. AEMO's 4,356 MW value is operational demand.

description: At 11:00 on 6 November NEM operational demand reached a record minimum of 11,892 MW, with distributed PV supplying approximately 45% of underlying demand.

During 13–19 November 2022, while South Australia was islanded following a transmission tower failure on 12 November, distributed PV was curtailed on 13–17 and 19 November to maintain operational demand. Curtailment reached approximately 410 MW on 17 November, which is a peak within the event window rather than the event date.
supporting_source_note: AEMO explicitly reports the demand-intervention period as 13–19 November. AER documents the related tower failure on 12 November and the seven-day South Australian islanding period.

description: At 13:00 on Easter Sunday 9 April NSW operational demand reached an all-time minimum of 4,101 MW.

A record-low-demand weekend affected the NEM on 16-17 September. South Australian operational demand reached 21 MW on 16 September, with distributed PV supplying 98.5% of underlying demand; on 17 September NEM operational demand reached a record 11,393 MW, 499 MW below the prior NEM record.
supporting_source_note: The one-day-apart South Australian and NEM rows were consolidated into the exact two-day interval because AEMO presents both as part of the same late-quarter minimum-demand episode.

event_name: NEM and NSW minimum demand record - 29 Oct 2023
description: On 29 October, NEM operational demand reached a record minimum of 11,009 MW and distributed PV supplied 51.3% of NEM underlying demand. New South Wales set a regional record of 3,719 MW on the same day, so both outcomes are recorded once at NEM level.
supporting_source_note: The separate New South Wales row was removed because AEMO reports the NEM and NSW records together on the same date and attributes both to high distributed-PV output.

event_name: SA first negative operational demand - 31 Dec 2023
description: At 13:30 on 31 December South Australian operational demand reached minus 26 MW, the first negative operational-demand interval recorded in the NEM; distributed PV supplied 101.7% of underlying demand.
supporting_source_note: Same 31 December event: AER reports minus 19 MW daily minimum native demand, while AEMO reports minus 26 MW operational demand. AER identifies rooftop solar output exceeding total regional demand.
